projects.name: Reel-finder: retrieval for half-remembered saved content
projects.oneLine: Search for saved content using canonical ingestion, deduplication, keyword and multilingual semantic retrieval. Feedback and coverage checks make retrieval gaps inspectable. Personal production system; case study available.
built: A single ingestion gateway: adapters produce raw items, canonical resource keys deduplicate links, and separate sightings retain source context.
Text acquisition from available captions, transcripts, OCR and page text; a staged pipeline records coverage gaps and reasons for missing content.
SQLite FTS5 keyword retrieval and multilingual-e5-large embeddings combined with reciprocal-rank fusion, exposed through a Python/FastAPI web interface.
Feedback labels, saved items, filters and stage telemetry. Development used coding-agent assistance; implementation and model choices are assessed against recorded evidence.
checked: Source review confirms ingestion, retrieval and telemetry modules. Historical verification records distinguish actual application probes from unit tests.

Recorded hybrid MRR was 0.910 on a small single-user set of 70 agent-drafted, owner-confirmed queries. On a harder 62-query content-answerable note set, with notes excluded from the index, hybrid MRR was 0.496. These are different development sets, not a held-out public benchmark.
The latest recorded keyword/item probe passed on a scratch database. The standard hybrid probe failed after an embedding-model allocation error; that failure is unresolved in this showcase review.
notClaimed: Personal exports, messages, media, databases, logs and private repository source are not published here.
No multi-user adoption, production-scale reliability, independent held-out benchmark, or completed general multimodal pipeline is claimed.
The headline retrieval score does not establish performance on vague owner wording; missing transcripts, partial vector coverage and model-memory failures remain real limits.

projects.name: Local-first ledger: ingestion, review and data integrity
projects.oneLine: Preserves review decisions across refreshes in a local Python, React and SQLite workflow with staging, reconciliation, undo and backup/restore. Private application; synthetic-data case study.
built: A local Python backend and React interface with SQLite storage, document staging, review queues, transfer reconciliation and record provenance.
Human confirmation and undo for ambiguous matches, with saved decisions protected from automatic refreshes.
Synthetic-data demo generation, verified-backup and restore tooling, integrity checks and a loopback-only application boundary.
checked: Reviewed the architecture, synthetic-demo procedure and dated verification records; no personal source records were opened for this showcase.

The project provides a scratch-database smoke flow and a combined verification script covering tests, health, backup restoration and decision locks. These are existing procedures, not a new verification run in this review.
notClaimed: No real account details, balances, transaction amounts, correspondents, private messages or screenshots of personal records are shared.
No financial-advice capability, automated money movement, complete reconciliation or universal statement coverage is claimed.
This is a personal local application developed with coding-agent assistance, not a public SaaS product or a scale benchmark.
